checks: A central grip translates and throws a card without inventing angular torque
An off-centre grip rotates beyond the old seven-degree wobble and release does not snap back
An off-centre release keeps angular momentum after the finger leaves
The eventual resting rotation is stored and matches the displayed face
Picking up a resting rotated card preserves its orientation
The grabbed point remains under the finger while the card rotates, including the original rotated local grip
Two fingers turn a card through more than one complete revolution without an angle-wrap jump or centre drift
The turning gesture does not scale card dimensions
Lifting the first finger transfers the grip to the remaining finger without ending the gesture
Compatibility clicks between finger releases cannot flip a card or open details during the remaining drag
The last finger releases normally, leaves no pointer capture and does not open card details
Lifting the second finger also continues a valid primary drag
Cancelling either finger restores the original pose and releases both captures without launching a throw
A spinning card can continue turning even when its linear release speed is zero
Holding the grip still before release suppresses an accidental old throw
Reduced motion disables automatic torque and release travel
Reduced motion still allows an intentional two-finger rotation
Q and E rotate by fifteen degrees, Shift uses forty-five, without triggering inspection
Rotated card corners stay fully inside the 1200×800 table, including portrait and landscape sizes
Rotated card corners stay fully inside the 844×390 table, including portrait and landscape sizes
Rotated card corners stay fully inside the 390×844 table, including portrait and landscape sizes
Rotated card corners stay fully inside the 320×480 table, including portrait and landscape sizes
An edge impact rebounds with lower linear and angular energy
Edge rebounds settle rather than tunnelling through the table or maintaining endless motion
The same off-centre motion at thirty, sixty and one hundred twenty samples per second produces nearly identical rotation and position
A stale animation frame after a background pause cancels momentum instead of resuming an old throw
scope: Actual shared title/story/ability table handlers and deterministic animation frames, torque, exact grip contact, two-finger angle unwrapping, pointer transfer and cancellation, manual keyboard rotation, reduced motion, spin-only throws, full rotated bounds, lossy collisions, sample-rate consistency and stale-frame cleanup in a controlled DOM. Browser pixels are not verified.
